category_title: Children with SEBN-B exhibiting external acting-out and disruptive behavior
student_description: This student exhibits external acting-out and disruptive behavior, often triggered by frustration when they cannot organize and convey their thoughts during peer interactions. The evidence reveals they uniquely need rigid linguistic structures to reduce the cognitive load of formulating arguments, alongside the autonomy to step away when emotionally overwhelmed. By providing strict conversational scaffolding and low-stakes entry points, the student can engage more reflectively and manage their frustration.

criteria.rationale: Sitting in a circle with the facilitator outside removes the pressure of an 'expert' and encourages direct peer-to-peer engagement.
criteria.check: The long-term plan includes arranging the physical environment so that all participants are equidistant and face one another, removing the tutor from a central authority position.

criteria.rationale: Having the student read a stimulus passage aloud provides a predictable, structured way to make their first contribution, building confidence for harder tasks.
criteria.check: The long-term plan incorporates routine, low-stakes participation tasks (such as reading a passage aloud) at the start of sessions to ease the student into engaging.

criteria.rationale: Discussing the student's experiences during normal, non-conflict moments helps them process their feelings and transfers reflective skills outside of high-pressure dialogues.
criteria.check: The long-term plan includes scheduling informal check-ins or conversations about the student's experiences during regular, non-instructional times to build reflective capacity.
